“Thank you for joining us today, Mydeimos!” the host of the night show smiled at the rockstar that was sitting on the couch opposite of him. The bright lights focused on Mydei, making him squint before he schooled his expression and sent a little wave to the crowd.

The roar of applause made him pause for a second.

“Thank you for having me.”

“It’s been a long time since we talked, hadn’t it? Last I remember it was before you decided to go solo,” the interviewer said. “And now you’re here promoting your first ever album. Tell us, what made you decide to split off and do your own thing?”

Mydei pushed a stray lock of strawberry blond hair away from his forehead. “It was a mutual decision. My friends wanted to try something different and I wanted to continue singing. That’s all.”

“No big fights, no dramas. You heard it here, folks,” the audience laughed. The host turned back to Mydei, “You’re still in contact with your ex-bandmates, then?”

“Of course,” Mydei nodded. “We’ve been friends since we were kids. Many of them are still involved in the industry, just behind the scenes.”

“Yes, I remember you mentioned in another interview that some of the songs on your new album were cowritten by your friends. Could you tell us more about your album?”

Mydei made himself comfortable in his seat. “I wanted to pay homage to the people who helped me get here. The album’s name, Strife, and each song has its meaning and a story behind it. The album had been in the works for a long time – some of the songs I’ve written years ago and only now decided to release once I was sure of my decision,” he then looked at the audience and sent them a private smile. “This album is a combined effort of many people. I hope you like it.”

“It sounds like you poured a lot into it. Is there a song we might have to look out for? Your favourite, perhaps?” 

The rockstar thought for a second before he shook his head. “No. Each and every one is special in its own way. I cannot say that any of them is lesser than another.”

“Your answers make us more and more excited to listen to your album. April 17th everyone, get your wallets ready,” the audience cheered, obvious in their excitment. “Now, Mydeimos, speaking of your songs. There have been a few rumors flying around. Care to confirm them?” the host smiled good-naturedly, ready to drop the topic as soon as he saw the first signs of Mydei closing off.

Mydei raised his eyebrows, prompting him to continue.

The man nodded. “Your protentional collaborating with Hysilens, of course! Your fans have been buzzing with excitement ever since you two were spotted in the studio together.”

The rockstar blinked as if he was trying to remember what the other man was talking about. “Oh. That,” he chuckled. “Cannot say much, my lips are sealed. I guess you will have to wait and see.”

The audience and the host groaned in unison.

The interview continued, stretching for almost an hour. It was only after Mydei played a small part of his upcoming single and answered every fan question that was sent to the studio, that the host had finally asked:

“Now, Mydeimos, I’m sure you’ve seen the recent news about your colleague.”

A slight frown marred Mydei’s face. “Colleague?”

“Phainon Khaslana, of course!”

There was a moment of silence before the audience roared in excitement.

“Ah,” Mydei’s voice flattened. “Him.”

The host laughed. “I see the rivalry is still going strong.”

Mydei’s face changed slightly. He quickly schooled his expression and sent a slightly tight smile to the interviewer. “You could say that.”

“We’ve heard that one of your songs will be used in Phainon’s upcoming movie, Irontomb. You’ve posted a small part of it on your account before, the beat is rather dramatic!”

“This song –” Mydei touched one of the rings on his fingers. “Me and Phainon had worked a lot on it. It was hard to get the right feel for the melody. We changed the sound multiple times before we felt like it fit the theme and did the movie justice. It was… definitely an enlightening experience.”

“And how was it working with Phainon Khaslana?” the host asked eagerly. “It was the first time you two worked on a project alone, wasn’t it?”

“It was,” Mydei nodded. He continued, no trace of humor on his face. “He’s just as infuriating as he was in the past. But he’s competent and he knows what he wants – he is not one who’d settle for something less when he knows he can make it better. He is a perfectionist. It was a pleasure working with him, even if he made me want to rip my hair out every time he opened his mouth.”

“That’s,” the host laughed a tad awkwardly, “very sweet. You two sound close.”

Mydei shrugged. “I guess. We spent a lot of time together.”

And then finally the host got to the point. “So, as Phainon’s friend, is there anything you could tell us about Phainon’s wife?”

The rockstar raised his eyebrow, unimpressed. He didn't reply.

The interviewer laughed and threw his hands in mock defeat. He winked at the camera, “I tried.”

Mydei huffed. He shook his head, slightly exasperated. “I can only tell you this – they’ve been together for a long time and for now, they wish for their relationship to remain private.”

The host blinked, a little taken aback by Mydei’s answer. “You’ve met them?”

“Yes. There are only so many times you could visit someone’s home without getting to know at least some of their family.”

“…And your verdict?” the interviewer drawled out, trying to get some of the juicy details of the scandal that had shaken the whole internet.

“My verdict?” Mydei asked, confused.

“About Phainon’s wife.”

Mydei blinked. “I really don’t see how that’s relevant but they seem to love each other a lot,” he then looked straight into the camera, his gold eyes intent and lips pursed. “I wish them a lot of patience. Clearly, they will need it with a husband like that.”

The host clapped, breaking the slight tension that had built in the room. “Thank you, Mydeimos! I’m sure Phainon’s wife will be happy to hear your words of encouragement,” Mydei scoffed but the host barreled on. “Everyone, give it up for Mydeimos! The album Strife will come out in two weeks, on April 17th. We wish you all the best, thank you for staying with us until the end!”

“Phainon!”

“Phainon, look here!”

“Looking good!”

“Hold that pose!”

“Phainon! Here!”

The cameras went off as soon as Phainon stepped on the red carpet. Dressed in an impeccable dark blue suit that highlighted his broad shoulders and tapered waist, with his white hair artfully tousled the paparazzi and fans alike immediately started off shouting their questions.

It seemed as if the whole world was waiting for the premier of Irontomb, not only because the movie was set to become one of the highest grossing films of all time and was already critically acclaimed by the most heavy-handed critics but also because this was Phainon Khaslana’s first ever public appearance ever since he dropped the earth-shattering news of his marriage.

Phainon posed for a few moments and after exchanging a few words with his manager, he finally made way to the shark pool that was commonly known as paparazzi.

“Hi, everyone!” he smiled. The paparazzi’s cameras went off, so much so that Phainon had to shield his eyes from the camera flashes. Someone was already recording and asking questions. Then the second voice chimed in, then the third - one voice overlapping another, producing a cacophony so loud and incomprehensible it made Phainon’s PR smile twitch at the corners.

Another person shoved their colleagues out of the way and thrusted a notepad into Phainon’s face. The actor reeled back before the notepad smacked him in the face. “Whoa, okay there. No need to be so aggressive, buddy.”

He quickly signed on a few notepads, “There you go. Now, everyone please calm down. I cannot hear a word you’re saying. I’ll answer a few questions,” he pointed at the young woman in the middle of the crowd. “You. Let’s start with you.”

The camera flashes slowly died down but the videos kept rolling. The woman Phainon had pointed at looked like a deer in headlights before she schooled her expression and rattled off her questions, “Hi! Nexus Magazine. What are your expectations for the movie? People were speculating that Irontomb will be the first of the upcoming trilogy, are we to expect more from this possible franchise? Did you like working on this movie? Is anyone special joining you later or are you here alone?” and then before her breath run out, she quickly pressed on. “What suit are you wearing?”

Everyone stilled and looked at her, blinking rapidly at her onslaught of questions.

Phainon’s PR smile slowly slid down his face and was replaced by a genuine grin the longer she talked. He spoke up once he was sure that she was done. “Well, aren’t you sweet for asking all important questions at once. Thank you!”

“Let’s start with my expectations for the movie,” Phainon started as the blushing journalist scrambled to take out her recorder. “They are quite high! We worked hard on this film, everyone had put their all into it. You never know how the public will react to your work until you put yourself out there but personally, I’m very hopeful. Irontomb was a project that was planned a long time ago and we were very lucky to have such a supportive director and crew that guided us in the right direction. It was truly a pleasure to be on set and working with everyone!

Regarding your questions about a sequel,” Phainon touched a ring on his finger as he contemplated his answer. He shrugged, “Can’t say much! Everything will be announced at a later date but I can tell you one thing, the story of Irontomb is far from finished. That’s all I can say before my managers come here and wring my neck,” he laughed bashfully and rubbed his neck, prompting the journalists to laugh.

“Is anyone else joining you today?” the young woman repeated, her eyes sparkling when Phainon smiled down at her knowingly. The paparazzi held their breaths, waiting for the actor’s answer.

“You could say that,” he smiled a little indulgently. “My wife will be joining me later. A truly shy little thing, that one. You understand.”

Some of the journalists nodded sympathetically. “It must be a little unusual for her.”

Phainon lowered his eyes, his expression a little sad. “Yeah, something like this. Still getting used to all this glamour and attention.”

The journalists and paparazzi surprisingly kept their silence, waiting for Phainon to continue. But before he could open his mouth, a familiar voice came from the other side of the red carpet.

“Why do you all think he married a woman?”

Ignoring the shouts and the camera flashes that followed him as he stepped out of the car, Mydeimos quickly walked down the carpet. He had heard only a few snippets of what Phainon had said but it was enough for him to paint the general picture, especially once the journalist replied.  

He stopped behind Phainon’s shoulder, his red suit a nice contrast to Phainon’s blue. They’d make a very striking picture if it only wasn’t for the deep frown marring Mydei’s face.

The paparazzi and journalists, conscious about who exactly it was that had first told the world about Phainon Khaslana’s new partner, sharpened their pens, ready to take notes.

Still, a few couldn’t help but balk at his words. “But… Mr. Khaslana said ‘his wife’…”

Mydei pursued his lips, inexplicably annoyed. A light pink hue dusted his cheeks when he replied, “That’s because this is what Phainon calls him.”

The man in question silently listened as his colleague exposed his little secret. He beamed when everyone’s heads swirled to him for answers. “My wife doesn’t mind!”

“And how do you know about what he minds and what he doesn’t,” Mydei grumbled from the side.

The journalists jumped on this like hungry sharks smelling blood in the water. “You seem to know them well, Mydeimos.”

Mydei looked at them like they had just said something stupid. But before he could even utter a sound, Phainon swooped in. “Of course he does! He was at the wedding!”

Mydei elbowed him in the side but the damage was already done. The paparazzi and journalists alike started shouting questions, trying to get to the bottom of it now that Mydeimos, their seemingly main source on Phainon Khaslana’s wife, has appeared.

Phainon smiled and with one hand on Mydei’s lower back, he steered them back towards the main venue. “Okay, that should be enough. Thank you everyone!”

“Wait!” the poor journalist from the Nexus Magazine shouted after them. “What about your suit?”

“I don’t know the designer, my wife had chosen it for me!” Phainon had said over his shoulder. He pointed at the fragrant white lily that was pinned to his lapel with a bright grin. “That too came from him!”

“Hey,” Dio elbowed his colleague in the side. Alexander shooed him away without looking back. He shot a few more photos – Castorice has finally left her apartment! These pics with her sister will sell big – when he was once more rudely interrupted.

“Don’t you see that I’m busy?” he snapped, checking his photos. Fuck, the last one was blurry.

Dio ignored him. He smacked him on the shoulder again and with a slightly shaky finger he pointed at someone near the marble fountain. “…Isn’t that Khaslana?”

“What?” Alexander perked up, looking in the same direction Dio was pointing at. “There’s no one there, what are you talking –” he glanced back at his own target and cursed, “fuck, Castorice is gone! Here goes my bonus. Thanks a lot, man!”

Dio continued as if in a trance. “That’s him, right? I’m not hallucinating?”

The other man paused. “…The hell is your problem?”

“You don’t understand,” Dio muttered, almost maniac. “I’ve been monitoring him for months. And he has not slipped up even once since he announced his marriage. Old Iris doesn’t care how, she needs me to figure out who his wife is. Our magazine needs to be the first ones to release these news. This is my chance!”

He sprinted in Khaslana’s direction on the opposite side of the street as soon as he finished talking. He stared at the man with bloodshot eyes, almost delirious with the thought of finally being done with his assignment.

Alexander shook his head as he watched him. “Weirdo.”

The stocky man ignored his crazy colleague and quickly got his camera rolling, immediately focusing it on the actor that was smiling at someone beside him. Yeah, he saw Khaslana a few moments before Dio but he knew when to pick his battles. Now though thanks to his stupid colleague his target was gone; and who did Dio think he was, a rookie? Chances of Khaslana telling them about his wife were very low but people were always hungry for more news – and Khaslana walking around the Plaza with someone was still good enough if one knew how to spin it correctly.

And Dio has given Alexander the chance to do so.

He involuntarily snorted when he saw Dio nearly get run over by a car and then went back to his camera. Whatever, it wasn’t like Dio was in much trouble. The boy was young and even if Khaslana wasn’t the biggest fan of paparazzi, he was always genial enough with them. Whoever was with him now couldn’t be much different.

And if they were, Alexander thought, Khaslana would know how to deal with it properly. The man was a born diplomat, the fuck was he even doing, wasting his time being an actor?

Alexander scoffed but the sound stuck in his throat when his eyes that were glued to the camera finally darted to the figure walking beside Khaslana and he saw who exactly was there. He immediately palled.

“Come back here!” he pushed his camera to the side and yelled after his colleague. “There’s someone with him!”

Dio jumped over a bush, nearly losing his footing in the process when his sneakers got caught on a spiky branch and yelled back. “More reason for me to be there!”

“No! Do you want to be fired? We have a no approach policy with –”

Alexander’s last words got lost in the wind and by the time Dio realized just who his colleague was warning him against, he had crossed the road and shoved a microphone into Phainon’s face.

“Mr. Khaslana!” Dio caught his breath and rattled off all of the questions his sleep deprived mind had come up with in the moment. “Nice weather we’re having, right? Do you visit this place a lot? Alone? Maybe with your wife? How is he, by the way? All fine with his health? He hasn’t appeared in public since your announcement, we’re all very worried for his wellbeing, please send our regards. Can you please answer a few of the questions? How long have you been together? How did you meet? When and where exactly was your wedding? Was it a closed ceremony? How does your wife feel about you being an actor? Is he in the industry as well? How –” Dio chocked on his spit and only then noticed Phainon’s bewildered face. The actor's body was half-turned, one hand stretched out as if he was hiding someone behind his back.

Dio instantly perked up, his breath picking up once more in excitement. “Who do you have there? Is that your wife?”

Phainon furrowed his eyebrows, his jaw clenching in irritation. He was dressed in a discreet hoodie and had hidden his very recognizable white hair under a plain grey cap. It was clear the man did not expect to get jumped by paparazzi right in the middle of the day.

Before he could open his mouth, a deep voice came from behind his back.

“It’s just me,” Mydeimos had stepped out from behind Phainon, holding a cup of strawberry iced tea in his hand.

Dio’s smile froze.

“Oh,” he said weakly. His hands started sweating. “Mydeimos. What… What a nice surprise seeing you here...”

He was so getting fired, Dio thought as he eyes glazed over Mydeimos’ signature leather jacket. How the hell did he miss him?

No approach policy, you fucking idiot! a little Alexander yelled in his head. 

Dio was actually done for if the rumours about the Kremnos family ended up being true. He'd heard enough about their lawsuits to be scarred for life, he didn't need to live through it too.

Mydeimos sipped his tea, looking at him a little curiously. “Are you alright?”

“Peachy! Just –” Dio’s smile shook at the corners of his lips. His left eye twitched. Then his right one. “Peachy. How… how are you?”

“Okay,” Mydeimos nodded calmly. “Is there something you wished to ask?”

Right, Dio thought a little hysterically. He was here on the job.

Why the hell didn’t he listen to Alexander?

He shot a careful glance at Phainon’s pissed off face and broke out in cold sweat. Might as well. What did he have left to lose? Mydeimos had already seen him. There was no going back.

“I… Yes. For Mr. Khaslana. About… about his wife.”

Mydeimos’ face twitched, his cheeks coloring slightly. He coughed to the side and motioned to Phainon. “Go ahead.”

Phainon’s expression relaxed a little, losing its cold edge. “My wife, huh," his voice was calm and yet it was laced with chilliness when he addressed Dio. He shook his head, almost as if he couldn't believe he was actually saying it. “I know this invasion of privacy comes with fame but it was the first time I had asked the public to not get involved. I've tried to be patient with you guys and yet I’ve been accosted like this dozens of times on the street and even in the privacy of my own apartment building in these last few months. Is that what you consider privacy?” Not hearing a response, Phainon continued. “And now, you’re what, stalking me on my walk with my… with Mydeimos?”

“I wasn’t –,” Dio tried to choke out but Phainon wasn’t done.

“You want to know something about my wife? Fine. Here is one fact for you – my wife is an amazing cook. He makes the most delicious meals and right now you, yes, you specifically, are preventing me from having my dinner with my beloved. Is there, perhaps, something else you wish to know about my private life? Maybe at what time had I woken up? Or what I had for breakfast? What brand of underwear I prefer? Or are we free to go?” he asked, smiling pleasantly at Dio.

Seeing as he was not about to get a response, he turned to Mydeimos that was silently standing by his side. Gold eyes blinked up at him. “Come on. I think we’re done here.”

The two men were ready to leave when Alexander finally made it to the scene. His face was red, hair completely messed up when he grabbed his frozen colleague by the arm and smiled at Phainon and Mydeimos. “Sorry, gentlemen, hope my colleague didn’t bother you. He got overexcited, you see, he’s so young. Inexperienced! First time interviewing a big celebrity! The nerves got to his head. Apologies, we will be out of your way now. Please send our regards to your partners!”

He didn't give them a chance to reply - he ran off, dragging a slightly shaky Dio after him. Not noticing how the frown on Phainon’s face deepened and how he quietly repeated to an equally confused Mydeimos, “’Partners’? Since when do you even have –”

Alexander brought Dio to their previous hiding spot. With his heart beating a mile per minute, hair plastered to his forehead and eyes wild around the edges, he smacked Dio on the head with a hard hand.

“Next time you listen to me before you sprint off to hell. Today I was responsible for you but don’t you even think of doing it again and dragging me with you or I will file a complaint to the hag!”

Dio rubbed his aching head, ashamed.

“…How bad is it?” he asked hesitantly. 

“’How bad?’” Alexander scoffed at Dio’s miserable mug. “Praying that Mydeimos’ parents don’t sue the ever-loving fuck out of you would be a good start. Why the fuck do you think he’s one of the only celebrities we have a no approach order with? Mydeimos is the nepo baby of this industry. He won’t be the one making a fuss – despite what he looks like, he’s a pretty chill dude – but his parents are fucking sharks. How fucking bad do you think it is?” still a little miffed he shoved his camera into Dio’s hands. “Here. I got some good shots of your man, maybe this will save you from Old Iris’ wrath.”

Dio felt tears well up in his eyes. Still shaken, he cradled the camera to his chest as if it was the most precious gift anyone had ever given to him in his short life. “Thank you....”

“Don't thank me, I'm not doing this for you. I’d feel kinda bad if you were completely broke when Eurypon Kremnos comes knocking on your door.”

Dio stilled, his face losing all color.

“Yeah, that’s what I thought. Now pray Mydeimos doesn’t tattle on you to his mommy and daddy. Seriously, the fuck were you thinking?”
